**Commentary on Surah al-Muzzammil**

It is a Meccan surah.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir, who said: The Quraysh gathered in Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of Quraysh) and said: "Give this man a name by which people will be turned away from him." They said: "He is a soothsayer (kahin)." They said: "He is not a soothsayer." They said: "He is a madman." They said: "He is not a madman." They said: "He is a sorcerer." They said: "He is not a sorcerer." So the polytheists dispersed on that basis. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he wrapped himself in his garments and covered himself with them. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "O you who are wrapped (al-Muzzammil)! O you who are covered (al-Muddaththir)!"

Al-Bazzar then said: Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: a group of people of knowledge have narrated from him and accepted his narrations, but he reported hadiths that no one else corroborates. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2276 (Kashf al-Astar). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3408, through Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/130): "Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti is in its chain, and he is a liar."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The Exalted commands His Messenger ﷺ to abandon *tazammul*, which is wrapping oneself up and covering oneself during the night, and to rise to stand in prayer before his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as He says: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and they spend of what We have provided for them﴾ [As-Sajdah: 16]. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was obeying what Allah had commanded him concerning the night prayer, and it was obligatory upon him alone, as He says: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Al-Isra: 79]. Here He explains to him the amount he should stand, saying: ﴿O you who are wrapped, stand [in prayer] the night, except a little﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾ means "O you who are sleeping." Qatadah said: "al-Muzzammil" means one wrapped in his garments. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: It was revealed while he was wrapped in a qatifa (a thick woolen cloak).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾: He said: "O Muhammad, the Qur'an has been wrapped around you."

* *

His saying ﴿half of it﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the night." ﴿Or reduce from it a little, or add to it﴾ means: We commanded you to stand half the night, with a slight addition or a slight reduction; there is no blame upon you in that.

* *

His saying ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)﴾ means: recite it slowly and deliberately, for that aids in understanding the Qur'an and reflecting upon it. The Prophet ﷺ used to recite in this way, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. 'A'ishah said: He would recite a surah and make it measured, so that it would be longer than the longer of its two parts.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas: He was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "It was prolonged (madd)." Then he recited ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, prolonging "Bismillah," prolonging "al-Rahman," and prolonging "al-Rahim." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5046.]

Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Umm Salamah: She was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: "He would divide his recitation verse by verse: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment﴾." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi. [Musnad Ahmad (6/302); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4001; al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi, no. 299.]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It will be said to the companion of the Qur'an (the one who recites it): Recite and ascend, and recite measuredly as you used to recite in the world, for your station will be at the last verse you recite."

It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)." [Musnad Ahmad (2/192); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1464; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2914; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8056.]

We have already mentioned at the beginning of the tafsir (commentary) the hadiths indicating the recommendation of measured recitation and beautifying the voice in recitation, as came in the hadith: "Adorn the Qur'an with your voices," and "He is not of us who does not chant the Qur'an melodiously," and "Indeed, this one has been given a flute of the flutes of the family of Dawud," referring to Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: "If I had known that you were listening to my recitation, I would have embellished it for you with embellishment." [For these hadiths, see the section on the virtues of the Qur'an in the introduction.]

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Do not scatter it like the scattering of sand, nor rush through it like the rushing of poetry. Stop at its wonders, stir hearts with it, and let not the concern of any one of you be the end of the surah." Narrated by al-Baghawi. [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/215).]

Al-Bukhari said: Adam narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us: I heard Abu Wa'il say: A man came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "I recited al-Mufassal (the surahs from Qaf to the end) in one rak'ah tonight." He said: "Rushing, like the rushing of poetry! I know the paired surahs which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite together." Then he mentioned twenty surahs of al-Mufassal, two surahs in each rak'ah. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 775.]

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word﴾: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: That means acting upon it.

It was also said: it is heavy at the time of its revelation, due to its greatness. As Zayd ibn Thabit said: "It was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while his thigh was upon my thigh, and my thigh nearly broke." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4592.]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Amr ibn al-Walid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, do you feel the revelation?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I hear a ringing sound (salasil), then I become silent at that point. Whenever revelation comes to me, I think that my soul is about to depart." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad Ahmad (2/222).]

At the beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, from Malik, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah: al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How does revelation come to you?" He said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me; then it departs from me, and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says." 'A'ishah said: "I certainly saw him when revelation descended upon him on a very cold day, and it would depart from him while his forehead was dripping with sweat." This is the wording of that narration. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was on his riding-camel, it would strike its chest (jiran) with its dewlap." [Musnad Ahmad (6/118).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that when revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on his she-camel, she would lower her jiran (dewlap), and she could not move until he was relieved. [Tafsir al-Tabari (29/82).]

This is a *mursal* (a hadith in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain). The *jiran* is the inner part of the neck.

Ibn Jarir preferred that the word "heavy" applies to both aspects together, as 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy on the Day of Resurrection in the scales."

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "*Nasha'* means: it stood up in Ethiopia (habashah)."

'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: "The whole night is *nashi'ah*." Likewise Mujahid and others said. It is said: "*Nasha'*" when one rises from the night. In another narration from Mujahid: "after 'Isha'." Likewise said Abu Mijlaz, Qatadah, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir.

The meaning is that *nashi'at al-layl* (the rising of the night) refers to its hours and times, and every hour of it is called *nashi'ah*, which are its moments. The intended meaning is that standing in the night is more effective in harmonizing the heart and the tongue, and more complete for recitation. Therefore He says: ﴿more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾, meaning: more conducive to the mind's concentration in performing the recitation and understanding it than during the day, because the day is the time of people's dispersal, the noise of voices, and the times of livelihood.

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, the Hafiz, said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, that Anas ibn Malik recited this verse: "Indeed the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more correct in speech (aswab qilan)." A man said to him: "We recite it as ﴿and more upright in speech (aqwam qilan)﴾." He said: "Indeed *aswab*, *aqwam*, *ahya'* and *ashbah* of this are one and the same." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/88). The verifier noted from Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari that he said: "This hadith is not authentically reported from any of the people of knowledge, since it is based on al-A'mash's narration from Anas, and it is therefore *maqta'* (disconnected), not *muttasil* (connected), because al-A'mash saw Anas but did not hear from him."]

For this reason He says: ﴿Indeed, for you in the day is a long *sabh*﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, and 'Ata' ibn Abi Muslim said: "*Al-farágh* (free time) and sleep."

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Ibn Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Sufyan al-Thawri said: "A long free time."

Qatadah said: "Free time, and seeking, and returning."

Al-Suddi said: ﴿A long sabh﴾ means: much voluntary worship (tatawwu').

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, for you in the day [is] a long sabh﴾, said: "For your needs. So empty the night for your religion." He said: "This was when the night prayer was obligatory. Then Allah bestowed grace upon the servants, lightened it and removed it, and recited: ﴿Stand [in prayer] the night, except a little﴾ to the end of the verse. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night﴾ until He reached: ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾ [the night, half of it or a third of it]. Then came a broader and more expansive command, which lifted the obligation from him and from his ummah." Then he recited: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Al-Isra: 79]. Ibn Zayd said what he said, and this is as it is said.

The evidence for this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, where he said: Yahya narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'id ibn Hisham: that he divorced his wife, then set out for Madinah to sell a property he had there, intending to spend it on horses and weapons, and then to fight the Romans until he died. He met a group of his people, who told him that six men from among their people had wanted to do the same during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "Do you not have in me a good example?" (*uswah*) He forbade them from that. He then called witnesses to his taking back his wife. Then he returned to us and informed us that he had gone to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about the Witr (the odd-numbered final prayer). Ibn 'Abbas said: "Shall I not direct you to the most knowledgeable person on earth regarding the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Go to 'A'ishah, ask her, then come back to me and inform me of her answer to you."

He said: I came upon Hakim ibn Aflah and asked him to accompany me to her. He said: "I will not approach her, for I forbade her from speaking about these two factions (*al-Shi'atayn*), but she refused regarding them except to continue." So I swore an oath to him, and he came with me. We entered upon her, and she said: "Hakim?" and she recognised him. He said: "Yes." She said: "Who is this with you?" He said: "Sa'id ibn Hisham." She said: "Who is Hisham?" He said: "Ibn 'Amir." She said: she sought mercy for him and said: "What a fine man 'Amir was!"

I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the Qur'an." I was about to stand up, then the matter of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) night prayer occurred to me. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the standing (in prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Do you not recite this surah: ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed Allah made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions stood (in prayer) for a year until their feet swelled, and Allah held back its final part in heaven for twelve months. Then Allah sent down the relief at the end of this surah, so the night prayer became a voluntary act after having been obligatory."

I was about to stand up again, then the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) occurred to me. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "We would prepare his siwak and his water for purification. Allah would awaken him whenever He willed during the night. He would use the siwak, perform wudu', then pray eight rak'ahs, sitting only at the eighth. He would sit, mention his Lord, the Exalted, supplicate and seek forgiveness, then rise without giving the salam. Then he would pray the ninth, sit, praise his Lord, mention Him and supplicate, then give the salam aloud so that we could hear it. Then he would pray two rak'ahs while seated after the salam. That is eleven rak'ahs, my son. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grew old and became heavy, he would pray the Witr with seven, then pray two rak'ahs while seated after the salam. That is nine, my son. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a prayer, he loved to be consistent in it. If sleep, pain or sickness prevented him from the night prayer, he would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day. I do not know that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) recited the whole Qur'an in one night, nor that he stood in prayer the whole night until morning, nor that he fasted a complete month other than Ramadan."

I then went to Ibn 'Abbas and related to him her narration. He said: "She has spoken truthfully. If only I could enter upon her, I would go to her until she spoke to me directly, face to face."

This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in full. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from the hadith of Qatadah, with similar wording. (Musnad, 6/54; Sahih Muslim, no. 746.)

Another route from 'A'ishah on this meaning: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, both of them together, and the wording is that of Ibn Wakf': from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, Muhammad ibn Tahla' narrated to me, from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I used to make a mat for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pray upon at night. People heard of this and gathered, so he came out as one who was angry, and he was merciful towards them. He feared that the night prayer would be made obligatory upon them. He said: "O people, take upon yourselves only those deeds that you are able to bear, for Allah does not tire of rewarding until you tire of acting, and the best deeds are those that are done consistently." Then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O you wrapped in garments, stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little, half of it, or decrease from it a little, or add to it﴾, until a man would tie a rope and hold onto it. They remained in this state for eight months. Then Allah saw what they sought of His pleasure, had mercy on them, returned them to the obligatory prayer, and abandoned the night prayer. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79.)

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak. The hadith in the Sahih (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6465; Sahih Muslim, no. 782) is without the addition about the revelation of this surah. This context may give the impression that this surah was revealed at Madinah, but that is not the case; it is Meccan. His statement in this context that the interval between the revelation of its beginning and its end was eight months is strange, for it has already been mentioned in Ahmad's narration that the interval between them was one year.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Simak al-Hanafi, I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "The first thing revealed was the beginning of al-Muzzammil. They would stand in prayer about as much as they stood in Ramadan, and the interval between its beginning and its end was close to a year."

Thus Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Usamah, with the same chain. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/78.)

Al-Thawri and Muhammad ibn Bishr al-'Abdi both narrated from Mis'ar, from Simak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The interval between them was one year." Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same as this.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: When ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾ was revealed, they stood (in prayer) for a year until their feet and shins swelled, until ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾ was revealed. He said: Then people rested. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79.)

Al-Hasan al-Basri also said likewise.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: [Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to us] from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'd ibn Hisham, who said: I said to 'A'ishah: "Inform us about the standing (in prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you not recite: ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed, it was the standing of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, until their feet swelled, and its final part was held back in heaven for sixteen months. Then it was revealed."

Ma'mar said, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little﴾: they stood for a year or two years, until their shins and feet swelled. So Allah sent down its relief afterwards at the end of the surah.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, that is Ibn Jubayr, who said: When Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) remained in this state for ten years, standing in the night as He had commanded him, and a group of his companions stood with him. Then after ten years Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) almost two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾ until His words: ﴿And establish the prayer﴾. So Allah lightened it for them after ten years. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79; this is mursal.)

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from 'Amr ibn Rafi', from Ya'qub al-Qummi, with it.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿O you wrapped in garments, stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little, half of it, or decrease from it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an distinctly﴾: Allah commanded His Prophet and the believers to stand in the night except for a little. That was hard for the believers. Then Allah lightened it for them and had mercy on them, and after this He revealed: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel through the land﴾ until His words: ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾. So Allah widened it, and to Him belongs all praise, and did not restrict it.

* *

His words: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ mean: mention Him often, devote yourself to Him, and dedicate yourself to His worship when you are free from your occupations and the affairs of your worldly life that you need, as He said: ﴿So when you have finished, then labour (in worship)﴾ [al-Sharh 94:7], meaning: when you have finished your tasks, then exert yourself in His obedience and worship, so that you may be free of mind. This was said by Ibn Zayd, in meaning or something close to it.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih, 'Ata', al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ means: make your worship sincere for Him.

Al-Hasan said: Strive, and devote yourself to Him entirely.

Ibn Jarir said: The worshipper is called *mutabattil* (one who devotes himself), and from this is the hadith narrated that he forbade *tabattul*, meaning withdrawing into worship and abandoning marriage. (In one copy: "marriage" is written as "tazwij".)

* *

His words: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾ mean: He is the Owner and the Disposer of the easts and the wests; there is no deity except Him. Just as you have singled Him out for worship, single Him out for reliance (*tawakkul*). ﴿So take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾, as He said in another verse: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud 11:123], and as His words: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾. There are many verses with this meaning, in which there is a command to single out worship and obedience for Allah, and to specify reliance upon Him.

**Commentary on Surah al-Muzzammil**

It is a Meccan surah.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir, who said: The Quraysh gathered in Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of Quraysh) and said: "Give this man a name by which people will be turned away from him." They said: "He is a soothsayer (kahin)." They said: "He is not a soothsayer." They said: "He is a madman." They said: "He is not a madman." They said: "He is a sorcerer." They said: "He is not a sorcerer." So the polytheists dispersed on that basis. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he wrapped himself in his garments and covered himself with them. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "O you who are wrapped (al-Muzzammil)! O you who are covered (al-Muddaththir)!"

Al-Bazzar then said: Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: a group of people of knowledge have narrated from him and accepted his narrations, but he reported hadiths that no one else corroborates. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2276 (Kashf al-Astar). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3408, through Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/130): "Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti is in its chain, and he is a liar."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The Exalted commands His Messenger ﷺ to abandon *tazammul*, which is wrapping oneself up and covering oneself during the night, and to rise to stand in prayer before his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as He says: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and they spend of what We have provided for them﴾ [As-Sajdah: 16]. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was obeying what Allah had commanded him concerning the night prayer, and it was obligatory upon him alone, as He says: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Al-Isra: 79]. Here He explains to him the amount he should stand, saying: ﴿O you who are wrapped, stand [in prayer] the night, except a little﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾ means "O you who are sleeping." Qatadah said: "al-Muzzammil" means one wrapped in his garments. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: It was revealed while he was wrapped in a qatifa (a thick woolen cloak).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾: He said: "O Muhammad, the Qur'an has been wrapped around you."

* *

His saying ﴿half of it﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the night." ﴿Or reduce from it a little, or add to it﴾ means: We commanded you to stand half the night, with a slight addition or a slight reduction; there is no blame upon you in that.

* *

His saying ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)﴾ means: recite it slowly and deliberately, for that aids in understanding the Qur'an and reflecting upon it. The Prophet ﷺ used to recite in this way, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. 'A'ishah said: He would recite a surah and make it measured, so that it would be longer than the longer of its two parts.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas: He was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "It was prolonged (madd)." Then he recited ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, prolonging "Bismillah," prolonging "al-Rahman," and prolonging "al-Rahim." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5046.]

Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Umm Salamah: She was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: "He would divide his recitation verse by verse: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment﴾." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi. [Musnad Ahmad (6/302); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4001; al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi, no. 299.]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It will be said to the companion of the Qur'an (the one who recites it): Recite and ascend, and recite measuredly as you used to recite in the world, for your station will be at the last verse you recite."

It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)." [Musnad Ahmad (2/192); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1464; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2914; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8056.]

We have already mentioned at the beginning of the tafsir (commentary) the hadiths indicating the recommendation of measured recitation and beautifying the voice in recitation, as came in the hadith: "Adorn the Qur'an with your voices," and "He is not of us who does not chant the Qur'an melodiously," and "Indeed, this one has been given a flute of the flutes of the family of Dawud," referring to Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: "If I had known that you were listening to my recitation, I would have embellished it for you with embellishment." [For these hadiths, see the section on the virtues of the Qur'an in the introduction.]

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Do not scatter it like the scattering of sand, nor rush through it like the rushing of poetry. Stop at its wonders, stir hearts with it, and let not the concern of any one of you be the end of the surah." Narrated by al-Baghawi. [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/215).]

Al-Bukhari said: Adam narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us: I heard Abu Wa'il say: A man came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "I recited al-Mufassal (the surahs from Qaf to the end) in one rak'ah tonight." He said: "Rushing, like the rushing of poetry! I know the paired surahs which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite together." Then he mentioned twenty surahs of al-Mufassal, two surahs in each rak'ah. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 775.]

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word﴾: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: That means acting upon it.

It was also said: it is heavy at the time of its revelation, due to its greatness. As Zayd ibn Thabit said: "It was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while his thigh was upon my thigh, and my thigh nearly broke." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4592.]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Amr ibn al-Walid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, do you feel the revelation?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I hear a ringing sound (salasil), then I become silent at that point. Whenever revelation comes to me, I think that my soul is about to depart." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad Ahmad (2/222).]

At the beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, from Malik, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah: al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How does revelation come to you?" He said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me; then it departs from me, and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says." 'A'ishah said: "I certainly saw him when revelation descended upon him on a very cold day, and it would depart from him while his forehead was dripping with sweat." This is the wording of that narration. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was on his riding-camel, it would strike its chest (jiran) with its dewlap." [Musnad Ahmad (6/118).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that when revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on his she-camel, she would lower her jiran (dewlap), and she could not move until he was relieved. [Tafsir al-Tabari (29/82).]

This is a *mursal* (a hadith in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain). The *jiran* is the inner part of the neck.

Ibn Jarir preferred that the word "heavy" applies to both aspects together, as 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy on the Day of Resurrection in the scales."

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "*Nasha'* means: it stood up in Ethiopia (habashah)."

'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: "The whole night is *nashi'ah*." Likewise Mujahid and others said. It is said: "*Nasha'*" when one rises from the night. In another narration from Mujahid: "after 'Isha'." Likewise said Abu Mijlaz, Qatadah, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir.

The meaning is that *nashi'at al-layl* (the rising of the night) refers to its hours and times, and every hour of it is called *nashi'ah*, which are its moments. The intended meaning is that standing in the night is more effective in harmonizing the heart and the tongue, and more complete for recitation. Therefore He says: ﴿more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾, meaning: more conducive to the mind's concentration in performing the recitation and understanding it than during the day, because the day is the time of people's dispersal, the noise of voices, and the times of livelihood.

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, the Hafiz, said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, that Anas ibn Malik recited this verse: "Indeed the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more correct in speech (aswab qilan)." A man said to him: "We recite it as ﴿and more upright in speech (aqwam qilan)﴾." He said: "Indeed *aswab*, *aqwam*, *ahya'* and *ashbah* of this are one and the same." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/88). The verifier noted from Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari that he said: "This hadith is not authentically reported from any of the people of knowledge, since it is based on al-A'mash's narration from Anas, and it is therefore *maqta'* (disconnected), not *muttasil* (connected), because al-A'mash saw Anas but did not hear from him."]

For this reason He says: ﴿Indeed, for you in the day is a long *sabh*﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, and 'Ata' ibn Abi Muslim said: "*Al-farágh* (free time) and sleep."

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Ibn Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Sufyan al-Thawri said: "A long free time."

Qatadah said: "Free time, and seeking, and returning."

Al-Suddi said: ﴿A long sabh﴾ means: much voluntary worship (tatawwu').

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, for you in the day [is] a long sabh﴾, said: "For your needs. So empty the night for your religion." He said: "This was when the night prayer was obligatory. Then Allah bestowed grace upon the servants, lightened it and removed it, and recited: ﴿Stand [in prayer] the night, except a little﴾ to the end of the verse. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night﴾ until He reached: ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾ [the night, half of it or a third of it]. Then came a broader and more expansive command, which lifted the obligation from him and from his ummah." Then he recited: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Al-Isra: 79]. Ibn Zayd said what he said, and this is as it is said.

The evidence for this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, where he said: Yahya narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'id ibn Hisham: that he divorced his wife, then set out for Madinah to sell a property he had there, intending to spend it on horses and weapons, and then to fight the Romans until he died. He met a group of his people, who told him that six men from among their people had wanted to do the same during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "Do you not have in me a good example?" (*uswah*) He forbade them from that. He then called witnesses to his taking back his wife. Then he returned to us and informed us that he had gone to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about the Witr (the odd-numbered final prayer). Ibn 'Abbas said: "Shall I not direct you to the most knowledgeable person on earth regarding the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Go to 'A'ishah, ask her, then come back to me and inform me of her answer to you."

He said: I came upon Hakim ibn Aflah and asked him to accompany me to her. He said: "I will not approach her, for I forbade her from speaking about these two factions (*al-Shi'atayn*), but she refused regarding them except to continue." So I swore an oath to him, and he came with me. We entered upon her, and she said: "Hakim?" and she recognised him. He said: "Yes." She said: "Who is this with you?" He said: "Sa'id ibn Hisham." She said: "Who is Hisham?" He said: "Ibn 'Amir." She said: she sought mercy for him and said: "What a fine man 'Amir was!"

I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the Qur'an." I was about to stand up, then the matter of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) night prayer occurred to me. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the standing (in prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Do you not recite this surah: ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed Allah made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions stood (in prayer) for a year until their feet swelled, and Allah held back its final part in heaven for twelve months. Then Allah sent down the relief at the end of this surah, so the night prayer became a voluntary act after having been obligatory."

I was about to stand up again, then the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) occurred to me. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "We would prepare his siwak and his water for purification. Allah would awaken him whenever He willed during the night. He would use the siwak, perform wudu', then pray eight rak'ahs, sitting only at the eighth. He would sit, mention his Lord, the Exalted, supplicate and seek forgiveness, then rise without giving the salam. Then he would pray the ninth, sit, praise his Lord, mention Him and supplicate, then give the salam aloud so that we could hear it. Then he would pray two rak'ahs while seated after the salam. That is eleven rak'ahs, my son. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grew old and became heavy, he would pray the Witr with seven, then pray two rak'ahs while seated after the salam. That is nine, my son. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a prayer, he loved to be consistent in it. If sleep, pain or sickness prevented him from the night prayer, he would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day. I do not know that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) recited the whole Qur'an in one night, nor that he stood in prayer the whole night until morning, nor that he fasted a complete month other than Ramadan."

I then went to Ibn 'Abbas and related to him her narration. He said: "She has spoken truthfully. If only I could enter upon her, I would go to her until she spoke to me directly, face to face."

This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in full. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from the hadith of Qatadah, with similar wording. (Musnad, 6/54; Sahih Muslim, no. 746.)

Another route from 'A'ishah on this meaning: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, both of them together, and the wording is that of Ibn Wakf': from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, Muhammad ibn Tahla' narrated to me, from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I used to make a mat for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pray upon at night. People heard of this and gathered, so he came out as one who was angry, and he was merciful towards them. He feared that the night prayer would be made obligatory upon them. He said: "O people, take upon yourselves only those deeds that you are able to bear, for Allah does not tire of rewarding until you tire of acting, and the best deeds are those that are done consistently." Then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O you wrapped in garments, stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little, half of it, or decrease from it a little, or add to it﴾, until a man would tie a rope and hold onto it. They remained in this state for eight months. Then Allah saw what they sought of His pleasure, had mercy on them, returned them to the obligatory prayer, and abandoned the night prayer. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79.)

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak. The hadith in the Sahih (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6465; Sahih Muslim, no. 782) is without the addition about the revelation of this surah. This context may give the impression that this surah was revealed at Madinah, but that is not the case; it is Meccan. His statement in this context that the interval between the revelation of its beginning and its end was eight months is strange, for it has already been mentioned in Ahmad's narration that the interval between them was one year.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Simak al-Hanafi, I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "The first thing revealed was the beginning of al-Muzzammil. They would stand in prayer about as much as they stood in Ramadan, and the interval between its beginning and its end was close to a year."

Thus Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Usamah, with the same chain. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/78.)

Al-Thawri and Muhammad ibn Bishr al-'Abdi both narrated from Mis'ar, from Simak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The interval between them was one year." Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same as this.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: When ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾ was revealed, they stood (in prayer) for a year until their feet and shins swelled, until ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾ was revealed. He said: Then people rested. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79.)

Al-Hasan al-Basri also said likewise.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: [Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to us] from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'd ibn Hisham, who said: I said to 'A'ishah: "Inform us about the standing (in prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you not recite: ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed, it was the standing of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, until their feet swelled, and its final part was held back in heaven for sixteen months. Then it was revealed."

Ma'mar said, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little﴾: they stood for a year or two years, until their shins and feet swelled. So Allah sent down its relief afterwards at the end of the surah.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, that is Ibn Jubayr, who said: When Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) remained in this state for ten years, standing in the night as He had commanded him, and a group of his companions stood with him. Then after ten years Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) almost two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾ until His words: ﴿And establish the prayer﴾. So Allah lightened it for them after ten years. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79; this is mursal.)

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from 'Amr ibn Rafi', from Ya'qub al-Qummi, with it.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿O you wrapped in garments, stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little, half of it, or decrease from it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an distinctly﴾: Allah commanded His Prophet and the believers to stand in the night except for a little. That was hard for the believers. Then Allah lightened it for them and had mercy on them, and after this He revealed: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel through the land﴾ until His words: ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾. So Allah widened it, and to Him belongs all praise, and did not restrict it.

* *

His words: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ mean: mention Him often, devote yourself to Him, and dedicate yourself to His worship when you are free from your occupations and the affairs of your worldly life that you need, as He said: ﴿So when you have finished, then labour (in worship)﴾ [al-Sharh 94:7], meaning: when you have finished your tasks, then exert yourself in His obedience and worship, so that you may be free of mind. This was said by Ibn Zayd, in meaning or something close to it.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih, 'Ata', al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ means: make your worship sincere for Him.

Al-Hasan said: Strive, and devote yourself to Him entirely.

Ibn Jarir said: The worshipper is called *mutabattil* (one who devotes himself), and from this is the hadith narrated that he forbade *tabattul*, meaning withdrawing into worship and abandoning marriage. (In one copy: "marriage" is written as "tazwij".)

* *

His words: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾ mean: He is the Owner and the Disposer of the easts and the wests; there is no deity except Him. Just as you have singled Him out for worship, single Him out for reliance (*tawakkul*). ﴿So take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾, as He said in another verse: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud 11:123], and as His words: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾. There are many verses with this meaning, in which there is a command to single out worship and obedience for Allah, and to specify reliance upon Him.

**Commentary on Surah al-Muzzammil**

It is a Meccan surah.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir, who said: The Quraysh gathered in Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of Quraysh) and said: "Give this man a name by which people will be turned away from him." They said: "He is a soothsayer (kahin)." They said: "He is not a soothsayer." They said: "He is a madman." They said: "He is not a madman." They said: "He is a sorcerer." They said: "He is not a sorcerer." So the polytheists dispersed on that basis. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he wrapped himself in his garments and covered himself with them. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "O you who are wrapped (al-Muzzammil)! O you who are covered (al-Muddaththir)!"

Al-Bazzar then said: Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: a group of people of knowledge have narrated from him and accepted his narrations, but he reported hadiths that no one else corroborates. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2276 (Kashf al-Astar). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3408, through Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/130): "Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti is in its chain, and he is a liar."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The Exalted commands His Messenger ﷺ to abandon *tazammul*, which is wrapping oneself up and covering oneself during the night, and to rise to stand in prayer before his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as He says: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and they spend of what We have provided for them﴾ [As-Sajdah: 16]. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was obeying what Allah had commanded him concerning the night prayer, and it was obligatory upon him alone, as He says: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Al-Isra: 79]. Here He explains to him the amount he should stand, saying: ﴿O you who are wrapped, stand [in prayer] the night, except a little﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾ means "O you who are sleeping." Qatadah said: "al-Muzzammil" means one wrapped in his garments. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: It was revealed while he was wrapped in a qatifa (a thick woolen cloak).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾: He said: "O Muhammad, the Qur'an has been wrapped around you."

* *

His saying ﴿half of it﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the night." ﴿Or reduce from it a little, or add to it﴾ means: We commanded you to stand half the night, with a slight addition or a slight reduction; there is no blame upon you in that.

* *

His saying ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)﴾ means: recite it slowly and deliberately, for that aids in understanding the Qur'an and reflecting upon it. The Prophet ﷺ used to recite in this way, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. 'A'ishah said: He would recite a surah and make it measured, so that it would be longer than the longer of its two parts.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas: He was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "It was prolonged (madd)." Then he recited ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, prolonging "Bismillah," prolonging "al-Rahman," and prolonging "al-Rahim." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5046.]

Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Umm Salamah: She was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: "He would divide his recitation verse by verse: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment﴾." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi. [Musnad Ahmad (6/302); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4001; al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi, no. 299.]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It will be said to the companion of the Qur'an (the one who recites it): Recite and ascend, and recite measuredly as you used to recite in the world, for your station will be at the last verse you recite."

It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)." [Musnad Ahmad (2/192); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1464; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2914; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8056.]

We have already mentioned at the beginning of the tafsir (commentary) the hadiths indicating the recommendation of measured recitation and beautifying the voice in recitation, as came in the hadith: "Adorn the Qur'an with your voices," and "He is not of us who does not chant the Qur'an melodiously," and "Indeed, this one has been given a flute of the flutes of the family of Dawud," referring to Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: "If I had known that you were listening to my recitation, I would have embellished it for you with embellishment." [For these hadiths, see the section on the virtues of the Qur'an in the introduction.]

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Do not scatter it like the scattering of sand, nor rush through it like the rushing of poetry. Stop at its wonders, stir hearts with it, and let not the concern of any one of you be the end of the surah." Narrated by al-Baghawi. [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/215).]

Al-Bukhari said: Adam narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us: I heard Abu Wa'il say: A man came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "I recited al-Mufassal (the surahs from Qaf to the end) in one rak'ah tonight." He said: "Rushing, like the rushing of poetry! I know the paired surahs which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite together." Then he mentioned twenty surahs of al-Mufassal, two surahs in each rak'ah. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 775.]

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word﴾: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: That means acting upon it.

It was also said: it is heavy at the time of its revelation, due to its greatness. As Zayd ibn Thabit said: "It was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while his thigh was upon my thigh, and my thigh nearly broke." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4592.]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Amr ibn al-Walid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, do you feel the revelation?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I hear a ringing sound (salasil), then I become silent at that point. Whenever revelation comes to me, I think that my soul is about to depart." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad Ahmad (2/222).]

At the beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, from Malik, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah: al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How does revelation come to you?" He said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me; then it departs from me, and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says." 'A'ishah said: "I certainly saw him when revelation descended upon him on a very cold day, and it would depart from him while his forehead was dripping with sweat." This is the wording of that narration. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was on his riding-camel, it would strike its chest (jiran) with its dewlap." [Musnad Ahmad (6/118).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that when revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on his she-camel, she would lower her jiran (dewlap), and she could not move until he was relieved. [Tafsir al-Tabari (29/82).]

This is a *mursal* (a hadith in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain). The *jiran* is the inner part of the neck.

Ibn Jarir preferred that the word "heavy" applies to both aspects together, as 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy on the Day of Resurrection in the scales."

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "*Nasha'* means: it stood up in Ethiopia (habashah)."

'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: "The whole night is *nashi'ah*." Likewise Mujahid and others said. It is said: "*Nasha'*" when one rises from the night. In another narration from Mujahid: "after 'Isha'." Likewise said Abu Mijlaz, Qatadah, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir.

The meaning is that *nashi'at al-layl* (the rising of the night) refers to its hours and times, and every hour of it is called *nashi'ah*, which are its moments. The intended meaning is that standing in the night is more effective in harmonizing the heart and the tongue, and more complete for recitation. Therefore He says: ﴿more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾, meaning: more conducive to the mind's concentration in performing the recitation and understanding it than during the day, because the day is the time of people's dispersal, the noise of voices, and the times of livelihood.

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, the Hafiz, said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, that Anas ibn Malik recited this verse: "Indeed the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more correct in speech (aswab qilan)." A man said to him: "We recite it as ﴿and more upright in speech (aqwam qilan)﴾." He said: "Indeed *aswab*, *aqwam*, *ahya'* and *ashbah* of this are one and the same." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/88). The verifier noted from Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari that he said: "This hadith is not authentically reported from any of the people of knowledge, since it is based on al-A'mash's narration from Anas, and it is therefore *maqta'* (disconnected), not *muttasil* (connected), because al-A'mash saw Anas but did not hear from him."]

For this reason He says: ﴿Indeed, for you in the day is a long *sabh*﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, and 'Ata' ibn Abi Muslim said: "*Al-farágh* (free time) and sleep."

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Ibn Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Sufyan al-Thawri said: "A long free time."

Qatadah said: "Free time, and seeking, and returning."

Al-Suddi said: ﴿A long sabh﴾ means: much voluntary worship (tatawwu').

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, for you in the day [is] a long sabh﴾, said: "For your needs. So empty the night for your religion." He said: "This was when the night prayer was obligatory. Then Allah bestowed grace upon the servants, lightened it and removed it, and recited: ﴿Stand [in prayer] the night, except a little﴾ to the end of the verse. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night﴾ until He reached: ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾ [the night, half of it or a third of it]. Then came a broader and more expansive command, which lifted the obligation from him and from his ummah." Then he recited: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Al-Isra: 79]. Ibn Zayd said what he said, and this is as it is said.

The evidence for this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, where he said: Yahya narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'id ibn Hisham: that he divorced his wife, then set out for Madinah to sell a property he had there, intending to spend it on horses and weapons, and then to fight the Romans until he died. He met a group of his people, who told him that six men from among their people had wanted to do the same during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "Do you not have in me a good example?" (*uswah*) He forbade them from that. He then called witnesses to his taking back his wife. Then he returned to us and informed us that he had gone to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about the Witr (the odd-numbered final prayer). Ibn 'Abbas said: "Shall I not direct you to the most knowledgeable person on earth regarding the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Go to 'A'ishah, ask her, then come back to me and inform me of her answer to you."

He said: I came upon Hakim ibn Aflah and asked him to accompany me to her. He said: "I will not approach her, for I forbade her from speaking about these two factions (*al-Shi'atayn*), but she refused regarding them except to continue." So I swore an oath to him, and he came with me. We entered upon her, and she said: "Hakim?" and she recognised him. He said: "Yes." She said: "Who is this with you?" He said: "Sa'id ibn Hisham." She said: "Who is Hisham?" He said: "Ibn 'Amir." She said: she sought mercy for him and said: "What a fine man 'Amir was!"

I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the Qur'an." I was about to stand up, then the matter of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) night prayer occurred to me. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the standing (in prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Do you not recite this surah: ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed Allah made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions stood (in prayer) for a year until their feet swelled, and Allah held back its final part in heaven for twelve months. Then Allah sent down the relief at the end of this surah, so the night prayer became a voluntary act after having been obligatory."

I was about to stand up again, then the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) occurred to me. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, tell us about the Witr of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "We would prepare his siwak and his water for purification. Allah would awaken him whenever He willed during the night. He would use the siwak, perform wudu', then pray eight rak'ahs, sitting only at the eighth. He would sit, mention his Lord, the Exalted, supplicate and seek forgiveness, then rise without giving the salam. Then he would pray the ninth, sit, praise his Lord, mention Him and supplicate, then give the salam aloud so that we could hear it. Then he would pray two rak'ahs while seated after the salam. That is eleven rak'ahs, my son. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grew old and became heavy, he would pray the Witr with seven, then pray two rak'ahs while seated after the salam. That is nine, my son. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed a prayer, he loved to be consistent in it. If sleep, pain or sickness prevented him from the night prayer, he would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day. I do not know that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) recited the whole Qur'an in one night, nor that he stood in prayer the whole night until morning, nor that he fasted a complete month other than Ramadan."

I then went to Ibn 'Abbas and related to him her narration. He said: "She has spoken truthfully. If only I could enter upon her, I would go to her until she spoke to me directly, face to face."

This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in full. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih, from the hadith of Qatadah, with similar wording. (Musnad, 6/54; Sahih Muslim, no. 746.)

Another route from 'A'ishah on this meaning: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, both of them together, and the wording is that of Ibn Wakf': from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, Muhammad ibn Tahla' narrated to me, from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I used to make a mat for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pray upon at night. People heard of this and gathered, so he came out as one who was angry, and he was merciful towards them. He feared that the night prayer would be made obligatory upon them. He said: "O people, take upon yourselves only those deeds that you are able to bear, for Allah does not tire of rewarding until you tire of acting, and the best deeds are those that are done consistently." Then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O you wrapped in garments, stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little, half of it, or decrease from it a little, or add to it﴾, until a man would tie a rope and hold onto it. They remained in this state for eight months. Then Allah saw what they sought of His pleasure, had mercy on them, returned them to the obligatory prayer, and abandoned the night prayer. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79.)

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak. The hadith in the Sahih (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6465; Sahih Muslim, no. 782) is without the addition about the revelation of this surah. This context may give the impression that this surah was revealed at Madinah, but that is not the case; it is Meccan. His statement in this context that the interval between the revelation of its beginning and its end was eight months is strange, for it has already been mentioned in Ahmad's narration that the interval between them was one year.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Simak al-Hanafi, I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "The first thing revealed was the beginning of al-Muzzammil. They would stand in prayer about as much as they stood in Ramadan, and the interval between its beginning and its end was close to a year."

Thus Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Usamah, with the same chain. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/78.)

Al-Thawri and Muhammad ibn Bishr al-'Abdi both narrated from Mis'ar, from Simak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The interval between them was one year." Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same as this.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: When ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾ was revealed, they stood (in prayer) for a year until their feet and shins swelled, until ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾ was revealed. He said: Then people rested. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79.)

Al-Hasan al-Basri also said likewise.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: [Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to us] from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'd ibn Hisham, who said: I said to 'A'ishah: "Inform us about the standing (in prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you not recite: ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾?" I said: "Yes." She said: "Indeed, it was the standing of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, until their feet swelled, and its final part was held back in heaven for sixteen months. Then it was revealed."

Ma'mar said, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little﴾: they stood for a year or two years, until their shins and feet swelled. So Allah sent down its relief afterwards at the end of the surah.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, that is Ibn Jubayr, who said: When Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) remained in this state for ten years, standing in the night as He had commanded him, and a group of his companions stood with him. Then after ten years Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) almost two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾ until His words: ﴿And establish the prayer﴾. So Allah lightened it for them after ten years. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 29/79; this is mursal.)

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from 'Amr ibn Rafi', from Ya'qub al-Qummi, with it.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿O you wrapped in garments, stand (in prayer) through the night, except for a little, half of it, or decrease from it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an distinctly﴾: Allah commanded His Prophet and the believers to stand in the night except for a little. That was hard for the believers. Then Allah lightened it for them and had mercy on them, and after this He revealed: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel through the land﴾ until His words: ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾. So Allah widened it, and to Him belongs all praise, and did not restrict it.

* *

His words: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ mean: mention Him often, devote yourself to Him, and dedicate yourself to His worship when you are free from your occupations and the affairs of your worldly life that you need, as He said: ﴿So when you have finished, then labour (in worship)﴾ [al-Sharh 94:7], meaning: when you have finished your tasks, then exert yourself in His obedience and worship, so that you may be free of mind. This was said by Ibn Zayd, in meaning or something close to it.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih, 'Ata', al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ means: make your worship sincere for Him.

Al-Hasan said: Strive, and devote yourself to Him entirely.

Ibn Jarir said: The worshipper is called *mutabattil* (one who devotes himself), and from this is the hadith narrated that he forbade *tabattul*, meaning withdrawing into worship and abandoning marriage. (In one copy: "marriage" is written as "tazwij".)

* *

His words: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾ mean: He is the Owner and the Disposer of the easts and the wests; there is no deity except Him. Just as you have singled Him out for worship, single Him out for reliance (*tawakkul*). ﴿So take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾, as He said in another verse: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud 11:123], and as His words: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾. There are many verses with this meaning, in which there is a command to single out worship and obedience for Allah, and to specify reliance upon Him.

**Commentary on Surah al-Muzzammil**

It is a Meccan surah.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir, who said: The Quraysh gathered in Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of Quraysh) and said: "Give this man a name by which people will be turned away from him." They said: "He is a soothsayer (kahin)." They said: "He is not a soothsayer." They said: "He is a madman." They said: "He is not a madman." They said: "He is a sorcerer." They said: "He is not a sorcerer." So the polytheists dispersed on that basis. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he wrapped himself in his garments and covered himself with them. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "O you who are wrapped (al-Muzzammil)! O you who are covered (al-Muddaththir)!"

Al-Bazzar then said: Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: a group of people of knowledge have narrated from him and accepted his narrations, but he reported hadiths that no one else corroborates. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2276 (Kashf al-Astar). It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3408, through Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/130): "Mu'alla ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti is in its chain, and he is a liar."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The Exalted commands His Messenger ﷺ to abandon *tazammul*, which is wrapping oneself up and covering oneself during the night, and to rise to stand in prayer before his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as He says: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and they spend of what We have provided for them﴾ [As-Sajdah: 16]. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was obeying what Allah had commanded him concerning the night prayer, and it was obligatory upon him alone, as He says: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Al-Isra: 79]. Here He explains to him the amount he should stand, saying: ﴿O you who are wrapped, stand [in prayer] the night, except a little﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾ means "O you who are sleeping." Qatadah said: "al-Muzzammil" means one wrapped in his garments. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: It was revealed while he was wrapped in a qatifa (a thick woolen cloak).

Shabib ibn Bishr narrated from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿O you who are wrapped﴾: He said: "O Muhammad, the Qur'an has been wrapped around you."

* *

His saying ﴿half of it﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the night." ﴿Or reduce from it a little, or add to it﴾ means: We commanded you to stand half the night, with a slight addition or a slight reduction; there is no blame upon you in that.

* *

His saying ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)﴾ means: recite it slowly and deliberately, for that aids in understanding the Qur'an and reflecting upon it. The Prophet ﷺ used to recite in this way, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. 'A'ishah said: He would recite a surah and make it measured, so that it would be longer than the longer of its two parts.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas: He was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "It was prolonged (madd)." Then he recited ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, prolonging "Bismillah," prolonging "al-Rahman," and prolonging "al-Rahim." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5046.]

Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Umm Salamah: She was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: "He would divide his recitation verse by verse: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment﴾." Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi. [Musnad Ahmad (6/302); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4001; al-Shama'il of al-Tirmidhi, no. 299.]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It will be said to the companion of the Qur'an (the one who recites it): Recite and ascend, and recite measuredly as you used to recite in the world, for your station will be at the last verse you recite."

It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)." [Musnad Ahmad (2/192); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1464; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2914; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8056.]

We have already mentioned at the beginning of the tafsir (commentary) the hadiths indicating the recommendation of measured recitation and beautifying the voice in recitation, as came in the hadith: "Adorn the Qur'an with your voices," and "He is not of us who does not chant the Qur'an melodiously," and "Indeed, this one has been given a flute of the flutes of the family of Dawud," referring to Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: "If I had known that you were listening to my recitation, I would have embellished it for you with embellishment." [For these hadiths, see the section on the virtues of the Qur'an in the introduction.]

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Do not scatter it like the scattering of sand, nor rush through it like the rushing of poetry. Stop at its wonders, stir hearts with it, and let not the concern of any one of you be the end of the surah." Narrated by al-Baghawi. [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/215).]

Al-Bukhari said: Adam narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us: I heard Abu Wa'il say: A man came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "I recited al-Mufassal (the surahs from Qaf to the end) in one rak'ah tonight." He said: "Rushing, like the rushing of poetry! I know the paired surahs which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite together." Then he mentioned twenty surahs of al-Mufassal, two surahs in each rak'ah. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 775.]

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word﴾: al-Hasan and Qatadah said: That means acting upon it.

It was also said: it is heavy at the time of its revelation, due to its greatness. As Zayd ibn Thabit said: "It was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while his thigh was upon my thigh, and my thigh nearly broke." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4592.]

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Amr ibn al-Walid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, do you feel the revelation?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I hear a ringing sound (salasil), then I become silent at that point. Whenever revelation comes to me, I think that my soul is about to depart." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad Ahmad (2/222).]

At the beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, from Malik, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah: al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How does revelation come to you?" He said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me; then it departs from me, and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says." 'A'ishah said: "I certainly saw him when revelation descended upon him on a very cold day, and it would depart from him while his forehead was dripping with sweat." This is the wording of that narration. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2.]

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was on his riding-camel, it would strike its chest (jiran) with its dewlap." [Musnad Ahmad (6/118).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that when revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on his she-camel, she would lower her jiran (dewlap), and she could not move until he was relieved. [Tafsir al-Tabari (29/82).]

This is a *mursal* (a hadith in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain). The *jiran* is the inner part of the neck.

Ibn Jarir preferred that the word "heavy" applies to both aspects together, as 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy on the Day of Resurrection in the scales."

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "*Nasha'* means: it stood up in Ethiopia (habashah)."

'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: "The whole night is *nashi'ah*." Likewise Mujahid and others said. It is said: "*Nasha'*" when one rises from the night. In another narration from Mujahid: "after 'Isha'." Likewise said Abu Mijlaz, Qatadah, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir.

The meaning is that *nashi'at al-layl* (the rising of the night) refers to its hours and times, and every hour of it is called *nashi'ah*, which are its moments. The intended meaning is that standing in the night is more effective in harmonizing the heart and the tongue, and more complete for recitation. Therefore He says: ﴿more effective in tread and more upright in speech﴾, meaning: more conducive to the mind's concentration in performing the recitation and understanding it than during the day, because the day is the time of people's dispersal, the noise of voices, and the times of livelihood.

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, the Hafiz, said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, that Anas ibn Malik recited this verse: "Indeed the rising of the night is more effective in tread and more correct in speech (aswab qilan)." A man said to him: "We recite it as ﴿and more upright in speech (aqwam qilan)﴾." He said: "Indeed *aswab*, *aqwam*, *ahya'* and *ashbah* of this are one and the same." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/88). The verifier noted from Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari that he said: "This hadith is not authentically reported from any of the people of knowledge, since it is based on al-A'mash's narration from Anas, and it is therefore *maqta'* (disconnected), not *muttasil* (connected), because al-A'mash saw Anas but did not hear from him."]

For this reason He says: ﴿Indeed, for you in the day is a long *sabh*﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, and 'Ata' ibn Abi Muslim said: "*Al-farágh* (free time) and sleep."

Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Ibn Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Sufyan al-Thawri said: "A long free time."
